headline: Southborough advanced a comprehensive addition-renovation design for Neary Elementary School while town boards confronted multi-million-dollar FY28 capital requests and operating deficits.
synopsis: In October 2026, the Elementary School Building Committee voted to advance a $38 million addition and renovation plan for Neary Elementary School after architects determined a $15 million baseline upgrade would leave major mechanical and educational needs unaddressed. Town boards simultaneously launched FY28 budget planning, with the Capital Improvement and Planning Committee vetting $2.15 million in capital requests and up to $49 million in long-term bonding amid warnings of potential operational overrides. School leaders also analyzed a projected $800,000 drop in regional debt service and potential employee health insurance savings to offset municipal fiscal pressures. Ahead of Special Town Meeting, the Community Preservation Committee voted to keep full funding for the Peninsula Trail pedestrian bridge on the warrant, while the Advisory Committee endorsed spending $240,000 to connect homes near the Parkerville Road landfill to town water. Planning officials extended their review deadline for the proposed Costco development to mid-December, and the Wastewater Study Committee partnered pro bono with an analytics firm to evaluate potential Route 9 disposal sites.

top_items.title: Neary School Option 3 advanced to schematic design
top_items.why: The Elementary School Building Committee voted 4-0 to advance an addition and renovation plan for Margaret A. Neary Elementary School to schematic design. Architects found a smaller $15 million upgrade would leave major mechanical and educational deficiencies unfunded due to building code mandates.
top_items.body: Following detailed cost analysis from Tappe Architects, the Elementary School Building Committee decided against a limited $15 million upgrade and unanimously advanced Option 3 for detailed design and cost modeling. Architects explained that after soft costs, contingency, and required fire sprinkler and accessibility upgrades, only $5.8 million would remain for direct repairs under the smaller scope, leaving boilers, unit ventilators, and educational enhancements unfunded. The committee directed Tappe to produce detailed schematic designs, exterior renderings, and comprehensive cost breakdowns covering site work, septic systems, and parking ahead of a November review and spring 2027 Town Meeting.

top_items.title: FY28 capital plan reviews $2.15 million in appropriations
top_items.why: The Capital Improvement and Planning Committee began evaluating preliminary FY28 requests comprising $2.152 million in direct appropriations and up to $49 million in bondable projects. Municipal and school leaders are coordinating to align requests against the town borrowing capacity.
top_items.body: The Capital Improvement and Planning Committee opened its review of departmental capital requests for fiscal year 2028, dominated by school proposals and heavy equipment replacements. Southborough public schools submitted $710,000 for building repairs including stairs, student sinks, and catch basin fencing, while Public Works sought multiple vehicle replacements. Committee members agreed to require department heads to present equipment inventories, lifecycle plans, and detailed quotes before assembling recommendations for a joint session with the Select Board and Advisory Committee.

top_items.title: Regional school FY28 capital and debt service outlook
top_items.why: Regional school subcommittees reviewed $460,000 in FY28 capital projects for Algonquin Regional High School and noted an expected $800,000 drop in debt service. Officials also evaluated healthcare changes that could yield $600,000 in operational savings.
top_items.body: School administrators presented five proposed FY28 capital projects totaling $460,000 for Algonquin Regional High School after correcting an arithmetic discrepancy in initial spreadsheets. Officials highlighted that the retirement of the 2004 high school renovation debt at the end of FY27 will produce a net reduction of approximately $800,000 in regional debt service, even with new borrowing for the athletic complex. District leaders warned of tight Proposition 2 1/2 limits in Southborough and Northborough and outlined plans to model level-service, level-funded, and 3% capped budget scenarios while negotiating health insurance changes.

top_items.title: Peninsula Trail pedestrian bridge funding advanced to Town Meeting
top_items.why: The Community Preservation Committee voted 3-2 to send the full $217,318 CPA funding request for the Peninsula Trail pedestrian bridge to Special Town Meeting without proposed cuts. The decision came despite earlier non-support votes from the Select Board and Advisory Committee.
top_items.body: The Community Preservation Committee debated whether to amend or scale back Warrant Article 4 for the October 17 Special Town Meeting, which requests $217,318 in additional CPA funding for a 65-foot footbridge along Route 30. Although members discussed an alternative floor amendment to eliminate contingency allowances and reduce the ask to $25,000, the committee opted by a 3-2 vote to present the article as originally written. Trails Committee members subsequently finalized voter outreach materials and presentations highlighting pedestrian safety and regional connectivity.

top_items.title: Planning Board extends decision deadline for Coslin Drive Costco
top_items.why: The Planning Board continued the public hearing on the proposed 167,000-square-foot Costco warehouse and 30-position fueling station to November 2, 2026. The board voted 5-0 to extend its statutory decision deadline to December 18, 2026, awaiting town peer reviews on traffic.
top_items.body: Due to ongoing consultant traffic peer reviews, the Planning Board postponed formal review of major site plan approval and special permit applications for the Costco development at 21 Coslin Drive. Board members voted unanimously to schedule a dedicated public hearing for November 2 and extended the statutory decision deadline through mid-December. Meanwhile, town officials announced that the governor signed special legislation authorizing Southborough to issue an additional off-premises liquor license for the site.

top_items.title: Advisory Committee backs landfill water main extension
top_items.why: The Advisory Committee voted 6-0 to recommend Article 7 at Special Town Meeting, approving $240,000 from water retained earnings. The project will connect two private residences near the closed Parkerville Road landfill to town water.
top_items.body: The Advisory Committee voted unanimously to recommend Town Meeting approval for Article 7 after confirming that the town will cover the full connection cost from the street into the private homes. Extending the municipal water main is designed to address contamination risks and avoid perpetual state-mandated well testing following chemical detections in monitoring wells near the capped landfill. The measure carries unanimous support from both the Select Board and Advisory Committee.

top_items.title: Pro bono parcel analysis approved for Route 9 wastewater
top_items.why: The Wastewater Study Committee voted 6-0 to partner with Artefacts AI on a pro bono analysis of town parcels for wastewater disposal. The study follows state confirmation that treated discharge in Zone C of the Sudbury Reservoir watershed is legally viable.
top_items.body: The Wastewater Study Committee authorized a pro bono collaboration with analytics firm Artefacts AI to identify and evaluate land parcels suitable for wastewater leaching fields along Route 9. The initiative uses public GIS and engineering data at no municipal cost to help locate the 15 to 20 acres required for a potential shared system. Committee members also reviewed guidance from the Massachusetts Department of Environmental Protection confirming that watershed discharge permitting is permissible under stringent water quality standards.
